security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel sets mstatus.MXR to make execute-only pages readable for user-memory access (copy_from_user/copy_to_user), but the MPT entry grants only X permission without R; the access faults unexpectedly because MXR does not override MPT permission interpretation — only the raw XWR bits in the leaf MPTE determine access, and MXR is explicitly excluded from MPT permission checks per step 7 sub-bullet.
security_spec.summary: MPT permission checks ignore mstatus.MXR and HLVX overrides; kernel MXR-based uaccess paths will fault on execute-only MPT entries where they would succeed under standard page-table MXR semantics, and KVM HLVX instruction emulation cannot bypass MPT execute-only restrictions.

findings.finding: Linux RISC-V does not define SR_MXR (bit 19, 0x00080000) anywhere in its CSR header. The only related bit defined is SR_SUM (bit 18, 0x00040000), which is used instead for supervisor user-memory access. No __enable_mxr(), set_mxr(), or any MXR manipulation code exists in arch/riscv/. The claimed vulnerability pattern — Linux setting mstatus.MXR for copy_from_user/copy_to_user — does not exist in this kernel.

spec_citations.excerpt: The MXR (Make eXecutable Readable) bit modifies the privilege with which loads access virtual memory. When MXR=0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1) will succeed. When MXR=1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed.

The MXR and SUM mechanisms only affect the interpretation of permissions encoded in page-table entries. In particular, they have no impact on whether access-fault exceptions are raised due to PMAs or PMP.

findings.finding: Linux RISC-V uses SR_SUM (bit 18), not MXR (bit 19), to enable supervisor access to user pages during copy_from_user/copy_to_user. The SUM mechanism is the correct RISC-V mechanism for this purpose. SUM allows S-mode to access U-mode pages; MXR is a different mechanism that makes execute-only pages readable. The two bits serve different purposes and Linux correctly uses SUM, not MXR, for user-memory access.
findings.snippet:
li t6, SR_SUM
csrs CSR_STATUS, t6
/* ... user memory access ... */
csrc CSR_STATUS, t6

spec_citations.excerpt: The SUM (permit Supervisor User Memory access) bit modifies the privilege with which S-mode loads and stores access virtual memory. When SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1) will fault. When SUM=1, these accesses are permitted.
